decisions.reason: After another year without negative signals, this rye country bread remains a low-cost close-to-core option, though overlap with other rye variants still creates some rationalization risk.
The premium raisin stollen is still the firm's flagship seasonal product and its award-backed reputation gives management little reason to withdraw it.
The rye mixed bread with seeds fits the established assortment well and can be kept on the market at low incremental cost while continuing to earn its place.
This dark barley malt rye bread is still inexpensive to offer, but its more niche taste profile and similarity to other rye launches make it the most likely bread candidate for later pruning.
The marzipan Christmas stollen is a natural seasonal extension in a German bakery-confectionery portfolio and, absent bad evidence, remains worth keeping for another season.
